page_title: How to build Chrome extensions with React + Parcel

sources.entry: Build A Chrome Extension with React + Parcel

summary.title: How to build Chrome extensions with React + Parcel
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a Chrome extension whose React app renders directly into the visited web page via a content script, using Parcel as the bundler and a popup button to trigger it.
keywords: how to make a chrome extension
takeaways: Create a manifest.json (manifest_version 2) with a browser_action popup and a content_scripts entry pointing at the bundled file.
Use Parcel's build and watch scripts to bundle React code into src/build/main.js.
Send a message from popup.js via chrome.tabs.sendMessage and listen for it with chrome.runtime.onMessage in the content script.
Inject a new div into document.body and render the React App into it with ReactDOM.render.
Load the unpacked project in chrome://extensions (Developer Mode) to test the extension.
summary.summary: The author walks through creating a Chrome extension whose React UI is injected into the visited web page rather than shown in a popup. The project uses a manifest.json with a popup and a content script, a package.json with Parcel build and watch scripts, and a popup button that sends an injectApp message to the content script. The content script then creates a div, appends it to the body, and renders a simple React component into it. The tutorial ends with instructions for loading the unpacked extension in Chrome and a link to a boilerplate GitHub repo.
